summary: This is a piece of a Maven pom.xml file, the configuration file that tells Maven which outside libraries a project needs. It adds Mockito, the library used to create stand-in "mock" objects such as a fake TemperatureSensor, so tests can run without real hardware.

lines.text: Opens the section of pom.xml where every external library the project relies on is listed; Maven downloads each one and places it on the classpath.
An XML comment marking the spot where the JUnit 5 entry already sits, so you can see that Mockito is being added alongside the existing test framework rather than replacing it.
Begins the description of one single library. Everything until the matching closing tag identifies which library and how it should be used.
Names the organisation that publishes the library, which keeps libraries from different vendors with similar names apart.
Names the specific package wanted from that organisation: mockito-core holds the mocking engine itself.
Pins an exact version so the build is reproducible and a future Mockito release cannot silently break your tests.
Restricts Mockito to test compilation and test runs only, so the mocking library is never bundled into the shipped application.
